summary: Carl Olson works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology, having studied under mentor John Y. Fenton. Affiliation records from 2005 to 2015 attest his post as Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College.

Carl Shigeo Yamamoto specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, also studying under Sonam Germano, William Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg, and under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. His career included posts at Schulpforta (~1865–1875), University of Jena (~1875–1903), and Trinity College Dublin.

Carl W. Ernst (born 1950) is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Stanford (~1968–1973) and Harvard (~1973–1981), later serving as professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill from 1992 to 2022.
Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (1876–1967) worked in linguistics and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht University (1917–1946), and taught Jan Gonda.

Carlo Giussani (1840–1900) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863) and under Giuseppe Bardelli, Albrecht Weber (1863), and Rudolf von Roth (~1864–1865).
Carlo Jamelle Harris works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin.

Carmen Blacker (1924–2009) specialized in Japanology and religious studies. She studied at Somerville College (~1947–1951) and under Shigeru Gorai, and served as Lecturer in Japanese at the University of Cambridge from circa 1955 to 1991.

Carmen Dragonetti (1937–2018) studied at the National University of San Marcos, working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She held posts at IIBS (1989), Nyingma Institute (1996), and Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (attested 2001).

Carmen Meinert works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. She earned a PhD from the University of Bonn by 2001 and held posts as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008) and Ruhr University Bochum.

Carol S. Anderson, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, earned her PhD at the University of Chicago and studied under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman. She served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

Carola Roloff (born 1959) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Hamburg (~1997–2003) under David P. Jackson, and held posts at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg and Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2006–2007).
Carola S. Carstens works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Rice University (1998–1999) and completed her doctorate at the University of Hamburg by 2005.

Carole McGranahan (born 1969) is a Tibetology and archaeology scholar. She studied at Colgate and Michigan (PhD 2001 under Nicholas B. Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler), joining the University of Colorado Boulder faculty around 2001.

Caroline A. F. Rhys Davids (1857–1942) studied at University College London and under T. W. Rhys Davids. Working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, she taught at Manchester and SOAS, and served as Pali Text Society President (~1923–1942).

Caroline Humphrey (born 1943) works in Iranian/Central Asian studies and religious studies. She studied at Girton College and under Edmund Leach, later holding posts at Scott Polar Research Institute (~1971–1977), Cambridge (~1978), King's College (~1978), and Michigan.

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is an archaeology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held posts as a Graduate Teaching Associate at Ohio State and Visiting Lecturer at Denison University (attested 1990).

Carson Schütze (born 1968) is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1992–1997). He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1997 and taught Edward Garrett.

Catherine Bell (1954–2008) worked in religious studies and sinology. She studied at the University of Chicago (~1977–1983) under Joseph Mitsuo Kitagawa and served as Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

Catherine Elaine Prueitt works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She received a BA from the University of Rochester (by 2007) and a PhD from Emory University (by 2016), studying under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton.
